items.q: A boy has recurrent bacterial chest infections after six months of age, absent tonsils and very low immunoglobulins of all classes. What is the defect?
o: Bruton tyrosine kinase mutation blocking B cell development
items.exp: X linked agammaglobulinaemia arrests B cell maturation through Bruton tyrosine kinase failure. Boys present once maternal IgG wanes, with absent B cells and tiny tonsils.
r: Incorrect. Oxidase failure causes granulomatous abscesses.
Correct. BTK mutation blocks B cell development.
Incorrect. Thymic failure mainly impairs T cells.
Incorrect. Complement failure favours Neisseria infection.
items.kp: Boy, absent tonsils, no immunoglobulin: Bruton disease.

items.q: Recurrent abscesses with Staphylococcus and Aspergillus plus granulomas and a failed oxidative burst test indicate what?
items.exp: Chronic granulomatous disease disables NADPH oxidase, so phagocytes cannot kill catalase positive organisms that destroy their own peroxide. Granulomas and abscesses follow.
r: Incorrect. IgA deficiency is often asymptomatic.
Correct. Failed burst plus catalase positive abscesses means this disease.
Incorrect. Hyper IgE adds eczema and skeletal features with high IgE.
Incorrect. C3 deficiency causes severe bacterial infection without this burst pattern.
items.kp: Catalase positive organisms expose a broken oxidative burst.

items.q: Conotruncal heart defect, hypocalcaemic seizures and low T cells in a newborn point to which deletion syndrome?
items.exp: DiGeorge syndrome from 22q11 deletion impairs thymus and parathyroid development, causing T cell deficiency and hypocalcaemia with conotruncal cardiac anomalies.
r: Correct. 22q11 deletion causes DiGeorge syndrome.
Incorrect. Down syndrome has a different cardiac and immune pattern.
Incorrect. Cri du chat does not cause this triad.
Incorrect. Turner syndrome affects girls with different features.
items.kp: Heart, calcium and T cells together mean DiGeorge.

items.q: An infant fails to thrive with oral thrush, Pneumocystis pneumonia, absent thymus and profound lymphopenia. Best diagnosis?
items.exp: Severe combined immunodeficiency collapses T cell immunity in early infancy, causing thrush, Pneumocystis and failure to thrive. Urgent stem cell transplant is life saving.
r: Incorrect. Bruton disease spares T cell opportunists like Pneumocystis.
Correct. Early opportunists plus lymphopenia mean combined deficiency.
Incorrect. IgA deficiency rarely causes this severity.
Incorrect. Angioedema is a complement regulator defect.
items.kp: Sick infant with opportunists: treat SCID as an emergency.

items.q: Adenosine deaminase deficiency causes combined immunodeficiency by which mechanism?
o: Loss of complement membrane attack complex
items.exp: Without adenosine deaminase, deoxyadenosine metabolites accumulate and poison developing lymphocytes, producing severe combined immunodeficiency. It was an early success for gene therapy.
r: Incorrect. Organ failure describes DiGeorge syndrome.
Correct. Metabolite toxicity destroys lymphocytes.
Incorrect. Complement loss causes Neisseria susceptibility.
Incorrect. Adhesion defects delay cord separation and cause abscesses without pus.
items.kp: ADA deficiency poisons lymphocytes from inside.

items.q: Which organism causes pneumonia most characteristically when HIV CD4 counts fall very low with gradual breathlessness and hypoxia?
items.exp: Pneumocystis pneumonia is the classic AIDS defining opportunist with subacute breathlessness, dry cough and hypoxia at low CD4 counts. Prophylaxis is standard at those levels.
r: Incorrect. Pneumococcus occurs earlier and more acutely.
Correct. Pneumocystis defines advanced HIV lung disease.
Incorrect. Haemophilus causes acute bacterial presentations.
Incorrect. Legionella follows water exposure with systemic features.
items.kp: Subacute hypoxic pneumonia in AIDS means Pneumocystis first.

items.q: Kaposi sarcoma in AIDS is driven by which virus?
items.exp: Human herpesvirus 8 drives Kaposi sarcoma, producing violaceous skin, oral and visceral lesions in advanced immunosuppression. Epstein Barr virus instead drives associated lymphomas.
r: Incorrect. EBV drives HIV associated lymphomas.
Correct. HHV 8 drives Kaposi sarcoma.
Incorrect. CMV causes retinitis and colitis in AIDS.
Incorrect. HPV causes warts and cervical neoplasia.
items.kp: Kaposi equals HHV 8 in every exam format.

items.q: Selective IgA deficiency most often presents how?
o: Absent tonsils with no B cells
items.exp: Selective IgA deficiency is the commonest primary antibody defect and is frequently asymptomatic, sometimes causing sinopulmonary or gut infections and associated autoimmunity or allergy.
r: Incorrect. Fatal opportunists suggest combined deficiency.
Correct. Most IgA deficient people are asymptomatic.
Incorrect. That pattern describes Bruton disease.
Incorrect. Neisseria suggests terminal complement deficiency.
items.kp: Commonest antibody defect is often silent: selective IgA.

items.q: Recurrent Neisseria meningitis in a teenager suggests deficiency of what?
o: Terminal complement components C5 to C9
items.exp: The membrane attack complex of terminal complement lyses Neisseria, so C5 to C9 deficiency causes recurrent neisserial infection despite otherwise preserved immunity.
r: Incorrect. IgA deficiency does not select Neisseria this way.
Correct. Terminal complement loss selects Neisseria.
Incorrect. Oxidase loss selects catalase positive abscess organisms.
Incorrect. BTK loss causes encapsulated bacterial infections.
items.kp: Recurrent Neisseria means check terminal complement.

items.q: Live BCG vaccine disseminates in an infant. Which defect is most likely?
items.exp: Live vaccines disseminate when T cell immunity is absent, as in severe combined immunodeficiency. BCG, rotavirus and oral polio vaccines are therefore withheld until immune status is known.
r: Incorrect. IgA deficiency tolerates live vaccines.
Correct. Disseminated BCG signals failed T cell immunity.
Incorrect. Complement defects do not disseminate BCG.
Incorrect. Spherocytosis is a red cell membrane disorder.
items.kp: Disseminated live vaccine equals cellular immune failure.
